topic: Poverty and government schemes — mixed tiers
description: MGNREGA, PMJDY, Ayushman Bharat, PMAY, Jan Dhan

questions.stem: MGNREGA — India's flagship rural employment scheme — guarantees how many days of work per household per year?

options.option_text: 50 days
100 days
180 days
365 days

questions.explanation: MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005) — legal right to 100 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household per year, on demand. World's largest public works scheme. During Covid (2020-21), the limit was raised to 150 days in drought-notified areas. Administered by the Ministry of Rural Development; wages are paid directly to bank accounts via DBT.

questions.stem: 'Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana' (PMJDY), launched in August 2014, is a flagship scheme for:

options.option_text: Housing for all
Financial inclusion (universal bank-account access)
Skill development
Road construction

questions.explanation: PMJDY — launched 28 August 2014 — brings every household into the formal banking system: a zero-balance savings account, RuPay debit card, overdraft facility, accident insurance. Over 50 crore accounts have been opened, ~₹2 trillion deposits (2024). The Jan-Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity underpins Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) for subsidies, reducing leakages.

questions.stem: 'Ayushman Bharat — Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana' (PM-JAY) offers beneficiary families annual health cover up to:

options.option_text: ₹1 lakh
₹5 lakh
₹10 lakh
₹2 lakh

questions.explanation: PM-JAY (launched 2018) — ₹5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation. Targets the bottom ~40 % of the population (identified via SECC 2011 deprivation criteria). World's largest government-funded health assurance scheme by coverage. Complemented by Ayushman Bharat Health & Wellness Centres (HWCs, for primary care) and the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).

questions.stem: The 'Multidimensional Poverty Index' used globally (and the Indian equivalent published by NITI Aayog) measures poverty across how many dimensions?

options.option_text: Two
Three
Five
Seven

questions.explanation: MPI's three dimensions — Health, Education, Standard of Living — covered by 10 indicators (nutrition, child mortality; years of schooling, school attendance; cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets). Developed by OPHI and UNDP's HDRO. NITI Aayog's National MPI adds bank account + maternal health. India's national MPI fell from ~25 % (2015-16) to ~15 % (2019-21) according to NITI Aayog.

questions.stem: India's 'Direct Benefit Transfer' (DBT) system depends on the JAM trinity. 'JAM' stands for:

options.option_text: Jobs, Agriculture, Markets
Jan Dhan, Aadhaar, Mobile
Justice, Administration, Media
Judiciary, Army, Ministry

questions.explanation: JAM trinity — Jan Dhan (bank account) + Aadhaar (biometric identity) + Mobile (SIM-linked) — enables secure, leakage-free Direct Benefit Transfer of subsidies (LPG, PM-KISAN, scholarships, etc.). Rolled out via DBT-Mission from 2013. Has cumulatively saved lakhs of crores from fake-beneficiary leakages.

questions.stem: 'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana' (PMAY) is a scheme for:

options.option_text: Skill development
Housing for all
Old-age pensions
Free electricity

questions.explanation: PMAY — launched 2015 — aims at 'Housing for All' through two sub-schemes: PMAY-Urban (for urban poor) and PMAY-Gramin (rural). Central assistance + CLSS (Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme) interest subsidies + pucca-house construction. Targets EWS, LIG, MIG groups. Goals refreshed for the 2024-29 period to build another 3 crore houses.

questions.stem: The National Food Security Act, 2013, covers approximately what percentage of India's population?
questions.explanation: NFSA 2013 entitles 75 % of rural + 50 % of urban population — ~67 % overall (~81 crore people) — to subsidised food grains (5 kg/person/month at ₹3/rice, ₹2/wheat, ₹1/coarse). Under PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (launched April 2020 during Covid), additional free grains were distributed; from Jan 2023, regular NFSA entitlement was made fully free for 5 years.

questions.stem: Under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY), each identified poorest-of-poor household is entitled to how many kilograms of subsidised foodgrain per month?

options.option_text: 25 kg of subsidised grain per household per month
35 kg of subsidised grain per household per month
45 kg of subsidised grain per household per month
5 kg of subsidised grain per person per month

questions.explanation: AAY households receive 35 kg of foodgrain per month at highly subsidised prices (₹2/kg wheat, ₹3/kg rice). Option D (5 kg per person) describes the Priority Household (PHH) entitlement under the National Food Security Act, 2013 — a very common mix-up in exams since both fall under the PDS umbrella.

questions.stem: The PM SVANidhi scheme, launched in June 2020 to restore livelihoods of urban street vendors, offered an initial collateral-free working capital loan of:

options.option_text: ₹5,000 as the first-cycle working capital loan
₹10,000 as the first-cycle working capital loan
₹20,000 as the first-cycle working capital loan
₹50,000 as the first-cycle working capital loan

questions.explanation: PM SVANidhi provides ₹10,000 as the first-cycle collateral-free working capital loan. On timely repayment, vendors qualify for ₹20,000 (second cycle) and ₹50,000 (third cycle). Candidates frequently confuse first-cycle (₹10,000) with second or third cycle amounts — the ₹20,000 option is the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: The Tendulkar Committee (2009) marked a methodological departure from the Lakdawala Committee's approach to poverty estimation. Which of the following best captures the key change?

options.option_text: It replaced consumption expenditure surveys with income-tax records for urban areas
It anchored the poverty line to a basket covering food, health, and education outlays
It adopted the World Bank's $1.25/day PPP threshold as India's official poverty line
It based rural poverty strictly on a daily caloric intake norm of 2,400 kcal per adult

questions.explanation: Tendulkar Committee shifted from calorie-norm anchoring to an MRP-based consumption basket incorporating private expenditure on food, clothing, education, and health — a broader welfare concept. Option D describes the older Lakdawala approach (2,400 kcal rural / 2,100 kcal urban), which Tendulkar explicitly replaced. Option C confuses it with international benchmarks that India never officially adopted.

questions.stem: The 'PM POSHAN Shakti Nirman Scheme' (formerly Mid-Day Meal Scheme, renamed 2021) provides free cooked meals to children studying up to which class in government and government-aided schools?

options.option_text: Up to Class 5 covering the primary stage of schooling
Up to Class 8 covering primary and upper-primary schooling
Up to Class 10 covering the secondary stage of schooling
Up to Class 12 covering senior secondary stage schooling

questions.explanation: PM POSHAN covers Classes 1–8 (primary and upper-primary levels) in government and government-aided schools. Many candidates recall only the original scope (Classes 1–5 / primary) before the scheme was expanded to include Classes 6–8. Option A is therefore the most tempting wrong answer.

questions.stem: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), which distributed free foodgrain over and above NFSA entitlements during COVID-19, was eventually:

options.option_text: Merged into Antyodaya Anna Yojana as an enhanced benefit tier
Subsumed into the National Food Security Act framework from January 2023
Extended indefinitely as a standalone post-COVID welfare programme
Transferred to states as a state-funded food subsidy programme

questions.explanation: From 1 January 2023, the central government merged PMGKAY into the NFSA framework, making free grain delivery to all NFSA beneficiaries the mainstream entitlement rather than a separate COVID-relief scheme. Option C is the most tempting distractor because PMGKAY was extended multiple times before finally being absorbed, leading many to assume it became permanent in its own right.

questions.stem: Under the Mahatma Gandhi NREGS Act, 2005, the mandatory social audit of every work taken up in a village must be conducted by the:

options.option_text: State Vigilance Committee once every three months at district level
Gram Sabha of the concerned village at least once every six months
Comptroller and Auditor General under a special performance audit mandate
Programme Officer at block level on a fixed annual calendar basis

questions.explanation: Section 17 of MGNREGA mandates that the Gram Sabha conduct a social audit of all projects in the village at least once every six months — a statutory community-oversight mechanism unique to this Act. The CAG distractor (option C) confuses social audits with performance audits; the Programme Officer distractor (option D) mislocates the authority to the block level; and the three-month frequency in option A mis-remembers the statutory interval.

questions.stem: Under the Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC) 2011, which of the following is an AUTOMATIC EXCLUSION criterion for rural households — making them ineligible for BPL welfare benefits?

options.option_text: Household has no literate adult member above 25 years of age
Household owns a motorised two-wheeler, three-wheeler, or car
Household head belongs to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe
Household has no adult male member between 16 and 59 years

questions.explanation: Owning a motorised 2/3/4-wheeler (or a fishing boat) is one of SECC 2011's automatic exclusion criteria, signalling economic capacity above the poverty threshold. Options C and D are automatic INCLUSION criteria — SC/ST status and female-headed households with no adult male aged 16–59 receive priority inclusion, not exclusion. Option A (no literate adult above 25) is also an auto-inclusion indicator. Candidates frequently confuse SECC's inclusion and exclusion lists, making all three distractors realistic error traps.
